text: The Badminton Asia Championships, previously known as the Asian Badminton Championships until 2006, is a tournament organized by Badminton Asia to determine the top badminton players in Asia. The event began in 1962 and has been held annually since 1991. Prior to 1994, the competition rotated between team and individual formats, but the team event was discontinued after that year. In 2003, a controversy arose when China withdrew from the tournament at the last minute; head coach Li Yongbo stated that the tournament did not award ranking points for the 2004 Summer Olympics and that the players needed more rest. Some of the top players also expressed interest in withdrawing due to the event's low competitiveness. The table provides an overview of all host cities and countries, with the most recent edition taking place in Ningbo in 2025. The number in parentheses indicates how many times that city or country has hosted the championships, and the number of events held at each location ranges from one to six, as listed in the right-most column. The list below includes players who have won both the Badminton Asia Championships and the BWF World Championships, achieving the title of both Asian Champion and World Champion. Another list highlights the most successful players in the tournament, with three or more gold medals. The categories are designated as MS (Men's singles), WS (Women's singles), MD (Men's doubles), WD (Women's doubles), and XD (Mixed doubles). The gold medal-winning teams are listed by year and country, with China being the most successful nation and the only one to achieve a full set of gold medals, which occurred in 2011.
